messages.subject: mapRegion 'latin america' cuts off part of Latin America - work around?
messages.subject_clean: mapRegion 'latin america' cuts off part of Latin America - work around?
messages.body_plain:
Note: posted to Stack Overflow with no luck. Sorry for the X-posting. (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/28838866/mapping-all-of-latin-america-with-rworldmap)

I am trying to plot some data for different countries in Latin America using the rworldmaps package. When including mapRegion='latin america', Mexico is cut off...is there any way to include Mexico other than by overriding using ylim and xlim? Thanks! EB

library(rworldmap)
df <- NULL
df$country <- c("Brazil","Mexico","Argentina")
df$code<-c("BRA", "MEX", "ARG")
df$popsize<-c(1000, 5000, 200)
df<-as.data.frame(df)
sPDF <- joinCountryData2Map( df, joinCode = "ISO3", nameJoinColumn = "code")
mapCountryData(sPDF, nameColumnToPlot="popsize", mapRegion='latin america')

messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] mapRegion 'latin america' cuts off part of Latin America - work around?
messages.subject_clean: [rworldmap group] mapRegion 'latin america' cuts off part of Latin America - work around?
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Emilio,

I just posted this to SO.

One way is to select out the countries you are interested in, get the bounding box for these using the bbox function, and then use that to specify the xlim and ylim.

Continuing from after your code:
#select out your countries
sPDFmyCountries <- sPDF[sPDF$NAME %in% df$country,]
#use the bbox to define xlim & ylim
mapCountryData(sPDF, nameColumnToPlot="popsize", xlim=bbox(sPDFmyCountries)[1,], ylim=bbox(sPDFmyCountries)[2,])

If you wanted just to display the boundaries of the countries you have (i.e. if you had all of the Latin American countries in your data) you could do :
mapCountryData(sPDFmyCountries, nameColumnToPlot="popsize")

Hope that helps.

messages.subject: Half degree grid
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

as I understand it is possible to create maps with a half degree grid (like the Köppen Map in the paper). Is it possible to retrieve an excelfile (or something that I can convert into an excelfile) that in three columns gives me the longitude, laditute and countrycode or name for each half grid?

Regards,
Patricia

messages.subject: Re: [rworldmap group] Half degree grid
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Patricia,
This should do what you ask.
Best wishes,
Andy

library(rworldmap)
#this is a grid with the UN numeric country code in each half degree cell
data(gridCountriesNumeric)

#convert the SpatialGridDataFrame to a dataframe of z,x,y
dF <- as.data.frame(gridCountriesNumeric)

#simple plot to check it looks about right
plot(dF$s1,dF$s2,col=dF$country.asc)

#output to a csv
write.csv(dF,"countryCodeGrid.csv",row.names=FALSE)

messages.subject: Former World Maps?
messages.body_plain:
Dear fellow rworldmap users,

Has anyone implemented a former map of the world, say from the relatively stable period 1949-1990, for example 1974 when the ISO 3166-1 was first published? This would be very useful when plotting historical data from this period. I understand that a lot of maps would be needed to cover the volatile 1990s and the time before 1949, but a few maps would cover the four decades between.

Any thoughts?

Best regards,

Magnus Palmblad

Leiden University
